definitions.meaning: A bounded commercial ability to author, instantiate, inspect, retrieve, and validate typed system material while preserving owner and authority boundaries.
The private candidate command surface for explicit DomainSpec authoring, linting, deterministic instantiation, and reproducible receipts.
The candidate read-only command surface for cataloging, snapshotting, retrieving, and natively validating explicitly registered ontologies.
Explicit DomainSpec-authored source whose identities, relationships, guards, failures, reads, writes, and effects remain inspectable and fail-closed.
Generation of one bounded target artifact from a selected closed realization with reproducible bytes and a baseline-bound receipt.
A deterministic content-addressed read model of one explicitly registered ontology package and its bounded records.
A reproducible record of exact inputs, artifacts, checks, outcomes, and claim ceiling that remains evidence rather than authority.
A bounded commercial right to use named CLI operations under explicit validity, user, project, usage, and revocation conditions.
An accountable boundary for customer source, generated artifacts, snapshots, and receipts with explicit confidentiality, retention, export, and deletion terms.
An exact reviewed binding from the stable commercial capability to versioned DomainSpec and Ontology CLI packages and their supported operations.

Customer-operated software that accepts one bounded request, validates an authored DomainSpec node, selects only its frozen supported meta-type realization, publishes to a new contained target, and returns exact artifacts and a receipt.

A typed request naming caller, entitlement, workspace authorization, validated project, authored node, supported language, new target, idempotency identity, and optional accepted integration binding without granting authority by itself.
A publication boundary that accepts only a normalized new target within the customer-authorized root and rejects existing, escaping, colliding, partial, or ambiguous targets.

A replaceable boundary that authenticates one KEP participant, preserves one versioned correlated exchange, and translates between KEP envelopes and the exact internal instantiation request and response without changing their meaning or authority.

A proposed versioned request, response, or failure carrier binding participant, correlation, idempotency, payload contract, timestamp or freshness posture, receipt references, omissions, and authority ceiling for one service exchange.

A separately owner-adopted KEP Product Capability and admitted ontology extension required before KEP may carry agent service invocation without widening the existing encrypted co-ownership capability.
